data.text:
**Claim 0: long lines at hundreds of thousands of volts, less heat loss**
- Energy Education (University of Calgary), Electrical transmission: overhead lines are very high voltage, between 100 kV and 800 kV, and do the majority of long distance transmission. URL: https://energyeducation.ca/encyclopedia/Electrical_transmission
- GAO report RED-76-107: higher voltage transmission allows reduction in the current required and therefore results in lower current losses. URL: https://www.gao.gov/assets/red-76-107.pdf
- Verdict: supported as written (100,000 to 800,000 volts).

**Claim 1: pole transformer 7,200 to 240/120 volts**
- Surplus Record listing, 15 kVA 7200 primary 240/120 secondary single phase polemount transformer. URL: https://surplusrecord.com/listing/15-kva-7200-pri-240-120-sec-1-phase-polemount-transformer-new-495087/
- NPC Electric, pole mounted transformer: converts primary voltages from 2.4 kV to 34.5 kV (including 12470GrdY/7200) to 120/240 V split phase. URL: https://npcelectric.com/transformers/pole-mounted-transformer
- Verdict: supported in a corrected form: a common pole transformer turns 7,200 volts into 240 and 120 volts (primary voltages range from 2,400 to 34,500).

**Claim 2: about 5 percent lost**
- EIA FAQ: annual electricity transmission and distribution losses averaged about 5% of the electricity transmitted and distributed in the United States in 2018 through 2022. URL: https://www.eia.gov/tools/faqs/faq.php?id=105&t=3
- Verdict: supported as written.
